etymologies.etymologyHTML: Borrowed from Latin lingua (“language”) +‎ -ist.

quote.citation: 1953, Samuel Beckett, Watt, 1st American edition, New York, N.Y.: Grove Press, published 1959, →OCLC:
quote.text: The words of these songs were either without meaning, or derived from an idiom with which Watt, a very fair linguist, had no acquaintance.

definitions.definition: A human translator; an interpreter, especially in the armed forces.
